analysis:
The supplied units are documentation-only CHANGELOG.md head text (lines 1265-1710), historical release notes. The patch excerpt shows the changed head range is 11-171, a new v0.10.4 candidate section, which is not visible in these units. The changed lines were therefore not directly examined, and they are beyond what these units cover. The visible text is unchanged historical content, and CHANGELOG.md contains no executable code, so it does not by itself create any authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or availability regression.

The historical notes touch several threat-model areas. They describe the encrypted SSD prefix cache and its write-budget ledger (T-041), App Attest worker and endpoint resumption (T-053, TB-011), logout and revocation (A-008), and official-build registration (T-054). None of these notes asserts a behavior that contradicts the canonical threat model.

The rollout note in the patch excerpt mentions prompt_anchor_mismatch quarantining a provider's cache affinity for up to 10 minutes when provider and coordinator disagree on Qwen JSON rendering. That is a coordinator-side availability and caching concern, and the code is not supplied. The note also says a constrained request disables MTP speculation for other requests in the same decode step, and that forced tool_choice is advertised only through tool_constraint_models. These are behavioral claims about code outside the supplied evidence. The next review pass should check the actual source changes for the Qwen grammar constraint path, the tool_choice advertisement gating, and the cache receipt handling, because the changelog alone cannot establish their security properties.

No finding is recorded. needs_deeper_review is set because the changed v0.10.4 section and the code it describes were not visible.
